brief: Goldman's Hedge Fund Trend Monitor tracks 1,001 funds with $5.1tn gross equity exposure entering Q4 2026. The AI trade's unwind has hit hedge funds hardest where they were most crowded: the Hedge Fund VIP basket of top long positions, tightly correlated with AI, is down 8% YTD and has lagged the S&P 500 by 14pp over six months, its worst six-month relative stretch in 20 years. In response funds cut leverage, pushing net long/short exposure to its lowest since Liberation Day and near pre-COVID lows, even as portfolio concentration and crowding rose to a record high, compounding the pain from the sell-off in popular names. Funds reacted by broadening out of TMT into both cyclical sectors (Financials, Consumer Discretionary, Industrials) and defensives (Consumer Staples, Utilities), and rotated within AI itself, adding to INTC and META while cutting GOOGL and QCOM; a majority of this quarter's biggest gainers in hedge fund popularity were non-AI names. Despite the VIP basket's drawdown, Goldman notes its concentrated-ownership strategies have historically outperformed in a majority of quarters since 2001.
